doc: Oracle records of the Morph M2 models (I12; format in the docstring of tests_m2/test_oracles.py and holon/gen/oracles.py). M2's Morph models are compiled from the M1 fact documents, which may not be edited (their hash is in every M1 statement), so this is a milestone-level sidecar: `facts` names the facts files it applies to, and holon.gen.oracles.Oracles.for_milestone gives it to every M2 model of them (audit M2/1 F-M2-11; the M2 facts of the extraction, spec/M2/facts/*.json, will find it as F/../../lib/oracles.json). A modelled entry's parameter is a parameter of the generated model, held as an oracle table (Bend function values are Type, never Data; the plan's fallback, BUILD_PLAN I12), and its hypothesis is a premise of the laws that need it: a CF premise over a finite set the law states (kind cf), or a hyp premise naming the hypothesis (kind hyp). An entry is modelled only when the facts call its parameter, so the model's transitions consult it; a stand-in the facts state inline stays inside the model, not_in_scope with the reason. Never global injectivity, never an axiom. A concrete instance only serves refutation and inhabitation (G11V). An entry may name, in real_oracle, an implementation of the real oracle available here, against which `holon oracle check` tests the hypothesis (A4). Covers the five M1 stand-ins (cited in ledger) and the whitepaper §11.1 oracle list.

hypothesis.doc: CF(agg, S) for every finite S: keccak256 over the blob versioned hashes of a batch (agg, version 2 headers) maps the elements of S to pairwise different values. Each law states its own finite S as a cf premise.

instance.doc: the M1 stand-in agg(xs) = AGG_BASE + enc(xs), injective (spec/M1/lib/morph_rollup.lib.json)

hypothesis.doc: CF(hdr_hash, S) for every finite S: keccak256 over a batch header's bytes (committedBatches[k] = keccak256(header)) maps the headers of S to pairwise different values, so a presented header whose hash equals the stored one is the stored header. Each law states its own finite S.

instance.doc: an injective encoding of the header's tokens: header equality, as the M1 model compares a presented header with the stored one (CF-keccak-headers)

oracles.reason: No fact document the M2 models are compiled from calls hdr_hash: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json compares a presented parent header with the stored batch by index and field equality (parent == lci and the stored csr == prev, Rollup.sol:312-314), never by hashing the header's bytes, so no M2 model transition consults this parameter. Routing it needs a facts document whose commit actions hash the presented header (the extracted facts, BUILD_PLAN I17-I20), not an edit of the M1 facts (audit M2/1 F-M2-11). Until then the stand-in stays inside the model (ledger CF-keccak-headers).

hypothesis.doc: isActive(a) holds exactly for the staked, unslashed submitters; challengeDeposit() = DEP; a lost challenge slashes, and so deactivates, the batch's submitter.

oracles.reason: ISubmitter is stateful: isActive changes with staking and with the slashing the rollup itself triggers (_challengerWin), so it is not a function of its arguments that a model could take as a parameter. M2 keeps the M1 stand-in inside the model (active-list membership, challengeDeposit = DEP, a slash removes the submitter from the active list; ledger oracle-ISubmitter) until the staking contract is extracted (BUILD_PLAN I36).

hypothesis.doc: The M1 verifier rule, IRollupVerifier.verifyAggregateProof as a stand-in that accepts iff proof == 1, on the proof tokens the models use: proof 1 is accepted and proof 2 is rejected (proof 0 never reaches the verifier: Rollup.sol:758 requires proof != 0). A rule of the stand-in, not a property of the real verifier.

oracles.reason: No fact document the M2 models are compiled from calls verify: spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json states the verifier as the inline guards ['==', 'proof', 1] (commitBatchWithProof, reason 22) and ['||', 'timeout', ['==', 'proof', 1]] (proveState, reason 22), src 'oracle: IRollupVerifier.verifyAggregateProof', so no M2 model transition consults this parameter and the proof == 1 rule is a stand-in inside the model. Routing it needs a facts document whose actions call verify(proof) (the extracted facts, BUILD_PLAN I17-I20), not an edit of the M1 facts (audit M2/1 F-M2-11). Until then the stand-in stays inside the model (ledger oracle-verifier); the hypothesis and its instance are kept as the record of that rule.

hypothesis.doc: sendMessage enqueues exactly one L1 message, at the next queue index.

oracles.reason: The messenger's modelled behaviour is a state update of the rollup's own message queue (sendMessage appends one message): part of the transition, not a value the model queries. M2 keeps the M1 stand-in inside the model (ledger oracle-messenger) until the messenger and the queue are extracted (BUILD_PLAN I36).

hypothesis.doc: Dec(Enc x ++ 0^k) = x: the batch compression codec decodes an encoding padded with zeros (whitepaper §8.5).

oracles.reason: No M2 model calls the compression codec: batch data are opaque tokens. The Go codec is modelled at loop granularity, with HypZ as its hypothesis, in BUILD_PLAN I38.

hypothesis.doc: The zkEVM circuits accept a batch proof only for a valid transition of its public input.

oracles.reason: The circuits are not modelled: the verifier entry's proof == 1 rule stands in for them. The public input and HypC are extracted in BUILD_PLAN I37.

hypothesis.doc: The KZG versioned hash of the all-zero blob, 0x01 || sha256(0xc0 || 0^47)[1:], is the value of ZERO_VERSIONED_HASH (Rollup.sol:25) and EmptyVersionedHash (common/blob/payload.go:22) (D2, whitepaper §11.6).

oracles.reason: KZG commitments and point-evaluation proofs are not model parameters: blob versioned hashes are opaque tokens in every M2 model. The one KZG fact a model uses, the zero blob's versioned hash (D2), is checked against the code by `holon oracle zero-blob` and recorded under Hyp-Z0-kzg in results/M2/hypotheses.json (ledger Hyp-Z0-kzg).

hypothesis.doc: The L2 transaction codec decodes every encoding it produces.

oracles.reason: Transactions are opaque tokens in every M2 model. The Go transaction codec is extracted with the Go frontend (BUILD_PLAN I18).

hypothesis.doc: The L2 predeploy contracts at their reserved addresses behave as specified.

oracles.reason: No M2 model reaches L2 state: the predeploys lie outside the M2 bundle (the L1 rollup contract and the batch data).

hypothesis.doc: The node's L1 fetcher returns the batch data and headers the chain committed, in order.

oracles.reason: The node's L1 fetcher lies outside the M2 bundle: the models take batch data as action inputs.

hypothesis.doc: The sequencer's sealing loop seals every block it is handed into a batch, in order, within the batch size bound.

oracles.reason: The sequencer's sealing loop is not modelled: batches enter the models as action inputs.
